thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 4198765432 - contbatch p99 tail breach in us-west2 - auto-page to #incidents. Metric: contbatch.p99_tokens = 2.3s (SLO 1.0s). Streaming stalls observed. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/incident/4198765432

sara: oncall here, looking. grabbing graphs now. any customer reports?

jon: i just saw a spike in p99 and a couple streaming timeouts on prod routes (chat and streaming). started paging.

ops-bot: Paging: @sara @jon @tariq. Initial severity: SLO-impacting. Auto-runbooks: contbatch-tail-triage, hedge-streaming.

sara: quick impact note - top customer traffic in us-west2, 6 customers w/ >1% error increase, one CS escalation pending (Acme Corp).

ellen-csm: Acme's support ticket 8742 shows degraded interactive responses since 14:13 PDT, they reported long freezes in streaming. on call for customer comms.

tariq: joining. early hypothesis: continuous-batching path creating oversized packs with mixed sequence lengths -> KV eviction jitter -> tail amplification.

jon: can we run a live query for batch size distribution and seq length histogram?

sara: running quick query on metrics: 
```
// prometheus-ish
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(contbatch_pack_size_bucket[1m])) by (le))
```
result: p99 pack_size ~= 48 (max configured 64), median ~8. seqlen skew: 1% of requests > 2048 tokens but they drive 30% of pack size.

tariq: that matches mixed-seqlen amplification. Streaming queues get long waits while giant seqs finish.

jon: mitigation ideas: 1) reduce max pack_size to 32, 2) enable seqlen-aware preemption (shed long queries into dedicated lane), 3) temporary hedge: route streaming to dedicated lower-latency pool or fall back to smaller quantized model variant.

sara: prefer quick config flip 1 + 3. reducing pack size is low-risk and fast. we can toggle routing later.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by sara: 
```
deploy apply contbatch.max_pack_size=32 --env=us-west2 --reason="live mitigation - tail p99" 
```
status: rolling -> started

jon: also toggling pack_evict_threshold from 0.8 -> 0.9? that might reduce premature KV churn. but careful, could increase memory.

tariq: i'd rather increase preempt weight for short requests temporarily: scheduler.weight.short += 0.2. that'll prioritize small requests and reduce tail.

sara: ok doing two steps in parallel: apply pack_size=32, and scheduler short-weight bump. i will run in us-west2 only.

deploy-bot: change applied: contbatch.max_pack_size=32 (us-west2). scheduler.short_weight +0.2 applied.

sara: monitoring p95/p99 now. initial p95: 420ms -> 210ms, p99: 2.3s -> 1.1s after the change. streaming stalls reduced from ~45/min -> ~6/min.

ellen-csm: told Acme we're investigating, ETA 15m for mitigation update. they asked if there's a workaround - we suggested using the api param "max_tokens" to limit very long requests for now.

jon: looks better but p99 still > SLO occasionally for a small slice of traffic. probably the long seqs still ride through. next step: create a canary route that routes large-seq requests to dedicated instances with packing disabled. non-invasive but needs routing tweak.

tariq: agree. can spin up 4 small dedicated carriers and route >1024 token requests there. I'll prepare a canary config.

sara: creating incident ticket and adding customer impact.

sara: notes for ticket: root cause suspected: mixed sequence-length packing causing tail amplification + KV eviction jitter under load. mitigation: reduced pack_size, increased short-request scheduler weight, hedged streaming to fallback model. status: partial mitigation, monitoring.

ops-bot: Incident status changed -> partial_mitigation. runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/contbatch-tail

jon: one more temp tweak: enable stream-hedge (duplicate first 64 tokens to streaming-fallback pool) for high-priority customers. low cost, reduces stalls while we stabilize.

ellen-csm: Acme on call, they asked if we have ETA on full fix. told them 2-4 hours and that we will follow up with technical postmortem. they appreciate the quick mitigation.

tariq: canary config ready: 
```
route:
  if request.seq_len > 1024:
    target: contbatch-dedicated-canary-usw2
    packing: disabled
```
spinning up instances now.

deploy-bot: canary instances provisioning started (4x gpus).

sara: p99 trending down further to ~0.95s after canary warm-up. streaming stalls < 2/min.

jon: customer-impact update: Acme degraded -> restored to near-normal. other 5 customers seeing reduction in errors.

ellen-csm: sending status update to Acme and to account slack. will keep them notified.

sara: decision: keep mitigations in place for now. next steps: 1) postmortem with packing telemetry; 2) longer-term: seqlen-aware pack cutoffs and smarter KV retention heuristics; 3) consider adaptive pack sizing per-tenant.

tariq: assigning action: imma own the postmortem and perf test for pack_size/seqlen policies. jon pls own the sched fairness tuning RFC.

jon: ack. will draft RFC and perf matrices.

lena: i start coverage in 20m and will take the handoff. will keep monitoring for next 2 hours.

sara: handing off to @lena. all mitigations documented in incident ticket 4198765432. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident 4198765432 status -> resolved (auto: metrics within SLO for 30m). summary: partial mitigations + canary routing applied, p99 returned to <1.0s. postmortem assigned to tariq.

lena: noted. will follow up in ticket and postmortem channel. closing channel for active ops.

ellen-csm: sending customer closure note.

sara: nice team work. follow-up items to track in the postmortem: exact traffic slices that caused amplification, KV eviction logs, and simulation of mixed seqlen loads.

jon: adding perf test jobs to reproduce. I'll attach scripts to the ticket.

ops-bot: resolved timestamp 4198765489.
